@@ -757,6 +757,7 @@ everything target-specific is independent.
 | D55 | Simplified-view idiom recognition (`DiagramNormalize`) always bails out on an action-bearing alternative | **`Railroad.diagramOf`'s `Simplified` branch now calls `DiagramNormalize.simplify`, which pattern-matches a rule's `Diagram.Stack` for two shapes — an alternative that's a strict prefix of another (rewritten to that prefix plus an `Optional` tail) and a stack of direct-left-recursive alternatives plus one base alternative (rewritten to `base` followed by a `ZeroOrMore` of the recursive tail(s)) — closing the "first shipped step" the railroad-renderer-roadmap's phase 4 already named as the target. `simplify` checks `hasAction(alts)` first and returns the diagram unchanged if any alt carries a `{% %}`/`{%? %}` `ActionCaption`: an action's evaluation order and binding belong to one specific alternative, and collapsing that alternative into a shared `Optional`/`ZeroOrMore` tail would silently relocate or drop it — a real bug caught before this landed (the drafted module, found already on disk uncommitted, had no such guard). Wider idioms — separated lists (`X (',' X)*`), general factorization, 3+-alternative stacks with no single recognized shape — are explicitly out of scope until they have the same kind of test-backed equivalence coverage; `source` stays byte-stable regardless of any of this, since only the `Simplified` branch calls `simplify` at all.** | Landing the "first shipped step" of an already-committed-to phase, not a new scope decision — the roadmap had named idiom recognition as the next milestone once the diagram AST and view plumbing existed; this is that step, scoped to exactly the two shapes with a real test (an obvious optional tail, a direct-left-recursive chain) rather than a broader factorization pass no equivalence-test suite yet backs (docs/railroad-renderer-roadmap.md's own "Non-goals" section records the broader restraint). |
 | D56 | `.gram.lock` records which `--diagram-view` produced committed artifacts, for provenance only | **A `diagramView` field on the sidecar `Lock`, following the exact optional/omit-when-default convention `sourceLayout` already established (D-numbered implicitly by that field's own prior addition): absent — and never written when `Source` — so every lock predating this field, and every lock `fmt` writes under the still-default `Source` view, keeps round-tripping byte-for-byte; present as `"diagramView": "simplified"` only when `--diagram-view=simplified` produced the committed sidecar SVGs. Like `sourceLayout`, `checkStructure`/`checkDrift` don't key on it at all — both classify a document from its fence content and headings alone, never from which view rendered a committed diagram, so this is maintainer-facing provenance, not a new gate.** | Closes a real, previously-silent gap: nothing on disk recorded which view produced a grammar's committed diagrams, so a maintainer (or a future audit) had no way to tell "simplified" from "source" short of re-running `fmt` and diffing. Deliberately not wired into `checkDrift` — the lock already has one established convention for a provenance-only field (`sourceLayout`), and this reuses it rather than inventing a second one. |
 | D57 | Railroad node navigation is shared code (`site/src/lab/railroadNav.ts`), bound to the renderer's own `data-rr-*` grouping | **Both the Lab and the Notebook island now bind nonterminal-node hover/click/keyboard navigation through one shared `bindRailroadNodeNav` helper, querying the `<g class="rr-node rr-node-nonterm" data-rr-kind="..." data-rr-label="...">` grouping `Railroad.scala`'s `renderSvg` already emits (railroad-renderer-roadmap's phase 3, "semantic affordances" — this is the "built from that structure" half that hadn't landed yet). The Lab's own hover/click cross-highlight (pre-existing) was migrated off querying `rect.rr-nonterm` plus its text sibling separately (two listener targets per node, because the text painted on top of the rect) onto one listener on the `<g>` itself. The Notebook, which had no diagram interactivity at all, gets the same click/keyboard "jump to that rule's cell" affordance the outline sidebar already had (`jumpToRule`, resolving a label to a block index the same way `jumpToOutlineEntry` does). Every click/keydown handler calls `stopPropagation()`, since both islands nest the diagram inside a larger click/keydown-handling container (a cell's own "click to edit" surface, in the Notebook's case) — activating a nonterminal reference must navigate, never also trigger the ancestor's own activation.** | The metadata already existed (per-node `<title>`/`data-rr-*`, shipped earlier) but nothing consumed it — the Lab's interactivity predated that metadata and was never migrated, and the Notebook never got equivalent interactivity built at all. One shared module rather than two islands growing their own subtly-diverging DOM-query logic; verified end-to-end against the real Scala.js engine (not mocked), including that navigating never also opens the source cell it navigated from. |
+| D58 | Real `---` YAML frontmatter for `.gram.md`, dual-read migration, threaded through lock + site nav | **A leading, `---`-delimited frontmatter block (`name:`/`lang:`, room for future keys) replaces the embedded fenced `` ```gramaire `` "General settings" block as the recommended way to declare a grammar's own metadata — chosen over extending the existing fence (the lower-migration-cost default a design debate recommended first) because the user explicitly wanted genuine frontmatter: free extensibility (lists/maps/quoting), standard tooling recognition (every markdown-aware editor/linter/static-site generator already special-cases a leading `---` block), and discoverability (metadata at byte offset 0, not buried in the Nth fence). Parsed by a new, deliberately minimal hand-rolled subset (`core/src/main/scala/gramaire/Frontmatter.scala`: flow scalars, quoted strings with backslash escapes, flow lists — no anchors, tags, multi-document, or block scalars) rather than a general YAML library, since `core` cross-builds to Scala.js (a JVM-only library like SnakeYAML can't) and the schema this project actually needs never exceeds this subset. `Frontmatter.strip` blanks the stripped lines to SAME-LENGTH space-padded text (not merely the same line count), so every downstream `SrcSpan`/diagnostic offset computed against the remaining document stays byte-for-byte correct with no caller-side adjustment. `Lr.scala` dual-reads for one release: a leading frontmatter block wins when present; otherwise the old fence still works, with a deprecation warning pointing at `gramaire fmt`. `gramaire fmt` gained a migration codemod (`GramaireCheck.migrateToFrontmatter`) that lifts `name:`/`lang:` out of the old fence into a new leading block and removes the fence (run once across every shipped example/grammar file in this same change). `Lock` gained an optional `name` field (populated from `Lr.nameOf`), following the exact omit-when-default provenance convention D56 established for `diagramView` — neither `checkStructure` nor `checkDrift` key on it. Sitewide, `parseMarkdownLite` (the one parser shared by the Notebook prose cell, Paper view, and PDF export) gained a frontmatter-skip step alongside its existing `<details>`/HTML-comment housekeeping skips, so the leading block never renders as a literal "--- name: X lang: Y ---" paragraph — this was the original, concretely-reported bug that motivated the whole change. `LabResponse` gained a `name` field (`Lr.nameOf`, read independent of whether the grammar notation parses) so the Notebook's download-source/download-PDF filename comes from the real frontmatter-aware name instead of a stale client-side `%name` regex that matched neither the old fence nor the new frontmatter format and always fell back to `"gramaire-notebook"`.** | Closes a concretely reported bug (frontmatter rendering as literal prose in Paper/PDF) and a design question ("how do I add real frontmatter, and how do the values reach the rest of the toolchain") in one pass, since fixing the render bug properly meant giving frontmatter a real parser and a real place in the pipeline rather than a narrow one-off text-skip. The dual-read window (one release, per this document's own migration-safety convention) means no `.gram.md` in the wild breaks the moment this ships; removing the old-fence fallback and its `knownSettingDirectives` machinery entirely is an explicit follow-up, not bundled here. Full YAML support was explicitly rejected as scope creep — the fixed, small schema Gramaire actually needs (`name`, `lang`, room to grow) never justifies anchors/tags/multi-document/block-scalar support, and a general library would break the Scala.js cross-build this project already depends on. |
